newsitem.title: SPAIN: Italy's Prodi says too early for cut in taxes.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says too early for cut in taxes.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Monday it was too early to imagine any fall in taxes, although an improvement in public finances would pave the way for such a move.
"I know very well that (Italy's) fiscal pressure is too high ... we are preparing to lighten the fiscal burden, but it is still too early," Prodi, in Madrid for the Nato summit, told reporters.

Asked to comment on the Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio's earlier statement that Italian investments are hampered by high taxes, he replied: "Fazio knows a reduction in the fiscal burden can only come when the economy is healthier."
On the EU approval of the Italian convergence plan, Prodi said: "the convergence plan was received well because it was right."

He said he wanted to assure EU partners that "they have nothing to fear, this is an ongoing policy and Italy has no intention of being virtuous for just one year but wants to be so in the future as well because the growth in employment and the future of the economy depends on it."
